skill.name: sending-emails
skill.description: Guides developers through Mailtrap live email sending with Email API, SMTP, transactional and bulk streams, batch sends, templates, SDK links, and common setup mistakes.
skill.summary: Choose and implement the correct Mailtrap path for live email sending.
skill.author: mailtrap

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, fenced curl examples, and official Mailtrap URLs. The live email sending capability is confirmed because the skill documents API and SMTP paths that can send external email when used with valid credentials. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden execution intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Live email examples can cause external side effects if executed with a real token.
remediation.suggestion: State that agents must get explicit user confirmation before running any live send command or SMTP test.

remediation.issue: Examples use production send endpoints throughout the guide.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note recommending sandbox testing or controlled recipients before any live transactional, bulk, or batch send.

remediation.issue: Bulk and promotional sending can create compliance and abuse risk.
remediation.suggestion: Add recipient consent, unsubscribe, and sending-domain compliance reminders near the bulk and campaigns sections.

content.value_statement: Mailtrap send paths can be confusing when transactional, bulk, batch, and campaigns overlap. This skill maps the right path and gives implementation references.
actual_capabilities: Helps choose platform integration, official SDK, HTTP Email API, or SMTP.
Explains transactional, bulk, batch, and campaigns sending paths.
Lists Mailtrap API hosts, SMTP hosts, ports, and token usage.
Provides curl examples for single, bulk, batch, and template sends.
Links official SDK repositories for Node.js, Python, PHP, Ruby, Java, .NET, and CLI.
Summarizes rate limits, suppressions, and common live sending mistakes.
limitations: It does not verify sending domains, tokens, or account permissions.
It does not send email by itself; live sends need valid Mailtrap credentials.
It does not cover sandbox testing, webhooks, or deliverability deep dives.
SDK method details must be checked against current SDK README files.

use_cases.title: Choose an integration path
use_cases.description: Compare Mailtrap platform integrations, SDKs, HTTP API, and SMTP for a new application.

use_cases.title: Configure operational email
use_cases.description: Set up password resets, receipts, alerts, and notifications on the correct transactional stream.

use_cases.title: Plan marketing volume
use_cases.description: Distinguish bulk, batch, and campaigns before sending promotional messages through Mailtrap.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Mailtrap send method
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose the right Mailtrap send method for my app. My platform is [platform], message type is [type], and volume is [volume].

prompt_templates.title: Set up transactional email
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through Mailtrap transactional email setup for [language or framework]. Include token handling, sender domain checks, and the preferred SDK or API path.

prompt_templates.title: Design a bulk or batch workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Mailtrap workflow for [message goal]. Decide whether I need bulk, batch, campaigns, or transactional sending, and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot live sending
prompt_templates.prompt: Help troubleshoot my Mailtrap live send issue. I use [API or SMTP], stream [transactional or bulk], error [error], and environment [environment].

output_examples.input: I need password reset emails from a Rails app.
output_examples.output: Use transactional sending. Prefer the official SDK if it supports your needed options, then verify the domain, token scope, sender, and recipient handling.

output_examples.input: We send weekly promotions to contacts stored in our own database.
output_examples.output: Use the bulk stream rather than the transactional host. Confirm consent, unsubscribe handling, token scope, and sending-domain setup before production sends.

output_examples.input: I need to hand off many different notification messages at once.
output_examples.output: Use batch on the correct stream. Batch reduces request overhead, but it does not change whether messages are transactional or promotional.

best_practices: Confirm the stream, recipient authorization, and sender domain before any live send.
Store Mailtrap tokens in environment variables and rotate them when access changes.
Test with sandbox or controlled recipients before bulk, batch, or production traffic.
anti_patterns: Sending promotional messages through the transactional host.
Running live curl examples with production tokens without user confirmation.
Guessing SDK constructors or method names instead of checking the current README.

faq.question: Is bulk the same as batch?
faq.answer: No. Bulk is a promotional sending stream. Batch is a way to submit many messages in one request.

faq.question: Can this skill send emails automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Live sends require valid credentials and explicit user action.

faq.question: Which integration path should I try first?
faq.answer: Use a platform integration when available, then an official SDK, then HTTP API, and SMTP only when needed.

faq.question: Does it cover SMTP settings?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists Mailtrap live and bulk SMTP hosts, ports, username behavior, and token-based password usage.

faq.question: Can I send template-based email?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explains when to use template UUIDs and points to the related template skill for details.

faq.question: Does this replace Mailtrap documentation?
faq.answer: No. It helps choose a path and links official docs and SDK repositories for current implementation details.
